title: pr-21789-optimize-cpu-request-path-thread-pinning-and-serialization
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We observed CPU-side request-path bottlenecks under high concurrency in the hosted and dedicated environments. Hot paths included request serialization/deserialization, a global thread-pool contention spike, and suboptimal scheduling of per-request work leading to poor cache locality and increased syscalls. This PR tackles multiple orthogonal CPU issues: (1) reduce serialization copies by switching to a zero-copy wire shim for internal RPC between frontends and runtime workers; (2) introduce per-core worker pools with CPU affinity (thread pinning) for the inference request path; (3) convert several mutex-protected team queues to lockless MPMC queues for enqueuing work to the inference engine; (4) delay heavy kernel-selection work until after lightweight routing decisions to avoid blocking the request thread; and (5) KV cache read-path improvements to use shared read-only pages and reduce refcount churn. Changes: - core/serve/request_path.cpp/.h: reworked the top-level request dispatcher to use a small fixed-size coroutine-like state machine and a zero-copy message view for request payloads. Removed an extra protobuf->json serialization pass we previously did for logging. - core/serve/thread_pool.{cpp,h}: new PerCoreWorkerPool abstraction that creates N worker groups pinned to distinct CPU sets; falls back to existing pool when pinning is disabled. Uses pthread_setaffinity on Linux and a best-effort wrapper for macOS. - core/serve/lockless_queue.h: added a bounded MPMC queue implementation (lockless), used for routing requests between acceptor threads and worker groups. - core/serve/kv_cache.cpp: introduced read-side snapshots for in-memory KV to avoid per-request locking; replaced atomic_shared_ptr churn with an epoch-based read barrier. - core/serve/kernel_selection.cpp: moved heavy heuristics to async stage and added a cheap fast-path that picks default kernels for common model families to avoid the scheduler hot path. - perf/bench/request_path_microbench.py: microbench harness and scripts used to measure tail-latency and throughput improvements. - docs/perf/notes-thread-pinning.md: notes for operators about environment flags and how to tune worker counts. Testing and results: - Microbenchmarks: 95th percentile latency for a 512-token request workload on c6i-large instances decreased from 72ms -> 44ms (-39%), p99 decreased from 210ms -> 130ms (-38%). Throughput improved ~2.1x at the same CPU utilization. - Production canary: rolled to a 5% traffic canary in 'us-west-2' for Redwood-hosted; observed similar tail-latency improvements and no error-rate regressions. - Unit & integration tests: added coverage for lockless queue edge cases, per-core pool lifecycle, and KV snapshot semantics. CI: initial CI run failed the perf benchmark gate due to a flaky test that depended on system load; the test was made deterministic and retried; final CI green. Rollout and config: - default behavior is opt-in via runtime flag --reqpath-percore-pool (off by default). - Added environment variables and README for ops: REDWOOD_REQPOOL_CORES, REDWOOD_REQPOOL_STRIDE, REDWOOD_DISABLE_PINNING. - Added a short migration note: the new zero-copy wire shim is backward compatible with existing frontends; however older custom integrations that relied on side-effectful serialization hooks should be tested (see release_notes). Related work: ENG-3124 (continuous batching follow-ups), ENG-3180 (kv_cache refactor). Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes to public REST/SDKs. Operators should review release notes before enabling pinning on heterogeneous hosts.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work. Can you add a short doc on expected CPU topology assumptions and fallback behavior when pinning fails? Also prefer std::atomic fence vs volatile in the queue implementation.
Aisha Patel: Added docs + updated queue fences to use atomic_thread_fence; expanded comments about fallback behavior.

Connor O'Neill: The per-core pool looks good. One question: have you measured throughput regression for small-model (<128 tokens) workloads? We should gate-by-default until we confirm no regressions on tiny requests.
Aisha Patel: Ran microbench for 64-token requests — latency unchanged, throughput +5%. Added results to perf notes and kept feature opt-in by default.
Lina Zhang: Approving after the flaky test fix and deterministic bench harness. CI green on rerun.
release_notes: Improved CPU request-path performance: lower tail latency and higher throughput by adding per-core worker pools (opt-in), lockless queues, zero-copy request wire shim, and KV cache read-snapshots. Opt-in via --reqpath-percore-pool. See docs/perf/notes-thread-pinning.md for tuning guidance and caveats.
notes: This PR groups multiple related optimizations into a single coherent rollout. We kept the changes behind flags and added detailed operator docs. The lockless queue is bounded; we added backpressure in the acceptor path to avoid unbounded memory growth. Follow-ups: automated NUMA-aware placement (ENG-3330) and per-tenant tuning telemetry (ENG-3342).
